entities.summary:
Donus was the bishop of Rome from 676 to his death on April 11, 678. This marked a crucial period in the papacy, as Donus navigated the complexities of the Byzantine Empire's influence over the Western Church.

The exact details surrounding Donus' life are scarce, but it is known that he played a significant role in maintaining the church's unity during a time of great turmoil. The Liber Pontificalis, a historical text detailing the lives of popes, provides limited insight into Donus' achievements and legacy.

Donus' tenure as bishop was marked by a series of diplomatic efforts aimed at strengthening ties between the Western Church and the Byzantine Empire. His successor, Pope Agatho, would go on to play a pivotal role in shaping the church's stance on the controversy surrounding the reign of Emperor Constantine V.

In conclusion, Donus' legacy as bishop of Rome was defined by his efforts to maintain stability within the church during a period of significant upheaval. His impact on the development of papal politics and diplomacy would be felt for centuries to come.

A key figure in the history of the Western Church, Donus remains an important yet somewhat overlooked chapter in the annals of ecclesiastical leadership.
